stories.headline: BRICS Foreign Ministers meet in New Delhi as Iran war and divisions test bloc unity, ends without joint statement
stories.summary: India hosted the BRICS Foreign Ministers meeting on May 14–15 in New Delhi, with Jaishankar chairing. Foreign ministers including Iran's Araghchi and Russia's Lavrov attended; the meeting ended without a joint statement after members failed to agree on the Iran war and West Asia crisis. Jaishankar called for safe Hormuz passage and zero tolerance on terrorism, while Araghchi told Jaishankar Iran would ensure maritime safety. NSA Doval separately met Araghchi. India also held bilateral talks on Russian crude oil amid imminent expiry of the US sanctions waiver.

stories.headline: Modi's five-nation tour — Netherlands stop: 17 agreements, Tata-ASML semiconductor deal, strategic partnership elevated
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi visited the Netherlands on May 15–16 as the second leg of his five-nation European tour, holding talks with Dutch PM Rob Jetten and signing 17 bilateral outcomes including a new India-Netherlands strategic partnership. Tata Electronics and ASML signed an agreement for a semiconductor fab in Gujarat. Modi also visited the Afsluitdijk dam and addressed the Indian diaspora in The Hague. Dutch PM Jetten separately raised a 2016 child abduction case. Jaishankar met Dutch FM Berendsen in parallel.

stories.headline: Modi's five-nation tour — UAE stop: strategic defence pact, $5B investment, energy security deals
stories.summary: On May 15, Modi visited Abu Dhabi on the first leg of his five-nation tour, signing multiple MOUs with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed including a strategic defence partnership framework covering maritime security and cyberdefence, oil storage agreements with ADNOC for up to 30 million barrels in Fujairah, and LPG supply deals. The UAE announced $5 billion in investment in Indian infrastructure. Modi publicly condemned recent attacks on the UAE and called for an open Strait of Hormuz. NSA Doval had pre-visit preparatory meetings in Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Modi's five-nation tour — Sweden stop: strategic partnership, Polar Star honour, EU industry engagement
stories.summary: Modi arrived in Sweden on May 17 for the third leg of his tour, upgrading India-Sweden relations to a strategic partnership and endorsing a joint action plan (2026–2030) on green transition, emerging technology, trade, security and defence. Modi was awarded Sweden's Royal Order of the Polar Star, his 31st international honour. He addressed the European Round Table for Industry alongside Swedish PM Kristersson and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

stories.headline: India hikes fuel prices 3 rupees per litre, imposes gold and silver import restrictions amid Iran war economic squeeze
stories.summary: India's state-run fuel retailers raised petrol and diesel prices by 3 rupees per litre on May 15 for the first time in four years, reflecting the economic strain from the Strait of Hormuz disruption. The government separately restricted silver imports and capped duty-free gold imports for jewellers. Modi, who had already appealed to citizens to adopt austerity measures including working from home and reducing foreign travel, denied reports of a foreign travel tax. The rupee hit a record low against the dollar and the RBI governor acknowledged further hikes may be needed.

stories.headline: US DOJ moves to drop criminal fraud charges against Gautam Adani; SEC civil case settled for $18 million
stories.summary: The US Justice Department is close to dropping criminal fraud charges against Gautam Adani filed in November 2024 over an alleged $265 million bribery scheme, after Adani hired a new legal team led by Trump's personal lawyer Robert Giuffra and pledged $10 billion in US investment. In parallel, Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani agreed to settle the SEC civil fraud lawsuit for $18 million without admitting wrongdoing. Multiple sources described an unusual DOJ meeting in April at which the investment pledge was presented.

stories.headline: Indian Army chief warns Pakistan 'choose geography or history'; military marks first anniversary of Operation Sindoor
stories.summary: Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi issued a sharp public warning to Pakistan on May 16, saying it must decide whether it wants to be 'part of geography or history' if it continues supporting terrorism. The statement came days after India marked the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor on May 7. CDS General Anil Chauhan stated Indian forces dominated every escalation ladder during Sindoor. Pakistan's ISPR sharply rebuked Dwivedi's remarks. US President Trump again repeated mediation claims, saying the India-Pakistan ceasefire was 'done as a favour' to Islamabad.

stories.headline: Amit Shah launches anti-narcotics push at RAW memorial lecture, announces first Captagon seizure
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah delivered the RN Kao Memorial Lecture at RAW on May 16, calling for a global war on drugs, uniform international laws, and real-time intelligence sharing to combat narco-terrorism. He set a goal of a 'Drug-Free India by 2047.' Separately, he announced that the Narcotics Control Bureau seized India's first-ever Captagon ('Jihadi Drug') consignment worth ₹182 crore under Operation RAGEPILL, arresting a Syrian national.

stories.headline: Amit Shah holds marathon Gujarat events on BJP election victories, tech park inaugurations, and dairy sector push
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah conducted a two-day Gujarat visit on May 17, inaugurating the 'Million Minds Tech Park' SEZ IT park in Ahmedabad, the Ganesh Real Estate Management Institute (GREMI), the National Institute of Design's Innovation Centre, and the Madhur Dairy plant. Shah made extensive political speeches citing BJP/NDA now governing 80% of India following West Bengal and Gujarat victories, criticised Congress leadership, and called for Gujarat to lead in AI, deep tech and service sectors.
